[[File:Tim Simon 2024 GEMPC.jpg|thumb|right|260px|[[2024 Eighth Annual GEMPC]].]]
'''Tim Simon''' (forums handle '''Aglets''')<ref name="pcchart">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/orgchart/orgchart.pdf PC organization chart] (PDF, created 6 May 2024), res.starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010210152/https://res.starwarsccg.org/orgchart/orgchart.pdf Internet Archive]</ref> played the [[2022 Regional Championships]].<ref name="reg22">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2022-06-2022-regional-championship-events/ 2022 Regional Championship Events], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020232529/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/2022-06-2022-regional-championship-events-bf.html Internet Archive]</ref> For the first issue of ''[[dGamer]]'' (January/February 2005) he wrote an overview of the tournament environment since the release of [[Virtual Set 8]], with a look at popular decks and new virtual cards.<ref name="tfn-dgamer">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_CCG_Covered_in_New_Decipher_Online_Magazine_89921.asp Star Wars CCG Covered in New Decipher Online Magazine], TheForce.Net (28 February 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050308013433/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_CCG_Covered_in_New_Decipher_Online_Magazine_89921.asp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pc-dl10-08">[http://www.swccgpc.com/downloads/category.php?id=10 Downloads: Player Articles and Newsletters], swccgpc.com (13 October 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081013105749/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/downloads/category.php?id=10 Internet Archive]</ref> Posting as Aglets, he organized the East Coast Open at Renaissance Games in Fallston, Maryland, on Saturday 2 April 2005, with guaranteed cash prizes and the Ultimate Prize pack.<ref name="pcf-4100-56761" /> He was the tournament director of the [[2006 Yavin IV Regional]] at Renaissance Games in Fallston on Saturday 1 April 2006, which he announced in February 2006 with a $15 entry fee, a guaranteed first prize of over $200, two byes to the 2006 World Championship and a virtual card design for the winner; his announcement recalled that the 2005 edition had drawn 26 players from at least eight states.<ref name="pcf-9009-123768" /> In June 2006 he posted the announcement of the [[2006 Maryland State Championship]] on 17 June 2006 at Renaissance Games, to be directed by [[Kevin Elia]].<ref name="pcf-10140-139455">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=139455#139455 MD States - 6/17/06], Tim Simon (Aglets), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (1 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618095754/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=10140&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref> He organized the [[2008 Delaware State Championship]] at Days of Knights in Newark, Delaware, on Sunday 14 September 2008, which he wrote might be the first sanctioned SWCCG qualifier ever held in Delaware,<ref name="pcf-22840-331255" /> and in November 2008 he posted the [[2008 World Championship]] decklists, completing the Day 3 lists on 26 November.<ref name="pcf-24244-354357">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=354357#354357 WORLDS 2008 DECKLISTS], Tim Simon (Aglets), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (26 November 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081207045343/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=355335&sid=da800f192a94d4e0badb0ea8628c4ff7 Internet Archive]</ref>

== Card credits ==
The printed credit lines of 3 [[Players Committee]] [[Virtual cards|Virtual card]]s name Tim Simon (3 original concept credits).<ref name="labels">[https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/0bc4377d9dd48a100625e0ec75de6032d2ea92a1/src/gemp-swccg-cards/src/main/resources/card_labels.json card_labels.json] in billbisco/swccg-gemp (commit 0bc4377d9): the printed labels of every Players Committee Virtual card, transcribed from the PC's card images. Field definitions: [https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/0bc4377d9dd48a100625e0ec75de6032d2ea92a1/docs/card_labels.md docs/card_labels.md].</ref> The credited cards are in [[Virtual Block 1]], [[Virtual Block 2]] and [[Virtual Set 2]], sets dated 2009–2015 on this wiki. The events named in the concept credits date from 2005 to 2006. The concept credits also name the event or award the concept came from: Pennsylvania States 2006 (1 card); New Jersey States 2005 (1 card). The full list of everyone credited is at [[Card Credits#Tim Simon|Card Credits]].
